problem: ns-gm currently has no concept of read-only vs write mode. All code executed via `ns-gm run` has full access to every NetSuite N/* module (including N/record, N/transaction, N/email, etc.) with no permission gating. The ticket requests a mechanism for an agent (Claude Code) operating in read-only mode to temporarily request write permissions for a single script, with human approval via a pop-up/UI window, scoped to that script only.

files.why: CLI entry point; all commands registered here (lines 14-92). New commands or flags for permission requests would be added here.
The run command client (lines 58-116). POSTs code to local proxy /run endpoint. This is the execution path that would need to be gated by a permission check.
Express proxy server. The /run endpoint (lines 35-86) forwards code to NetSuite RESTlet. No permission filtering or mode concept exists today.
OAuth 2.0 M2M authentication. Manages token cache and RESTlet calls (lines 135-207). Single credential profile used per request; no concept of permission levels.

Deployed NetSuite RESTlet. Executes arbitrary code via `new Function()` (line 166) with all N/* modules injected (lines 71-96). No server-side permission filtering. This is where write operations actually happen.
Credential alias store (~/.ns-gm/credentials.json). Profile shape has no permission/mode fields (lines 59-66). Would need extension if read/write profiles are differentiated.
Interactive setup flow. Creates/selects credential profiles. Would need changes if separate read-only and read-write profiles are managed.
Non-interactive setup used by helix-ns-server (lines 33-63). Same profile shape, no mode concept.
Starts the local Express proxy as detached process (lines 59-105). Proxy must be running for any execution. The proxy process is long-lived and stateless regarding permissions.
Proxy configuration (port 9292, inactivity timeout). No permission-related config exists.
Semantic exit codes for CLI (lines 8-16). No permission-denied exit code exists today.
Help system with JSON and text output formats. Would need updates for new commands/flags.
Product definition. Line 71 explicitly states 'No advanced profile permissions model in this phase' as a non-goal. This ticket changes that scope.
AI agent guidance document. Lists architecture, command surface, and active files. Would need updates for new permission workflow.
Dependencies include 'prompts' (terminal UI) and 'commander' (CLI). Node >=24.0.0. No GUI or web UI dependencies exist today.

facts: ns-gm is a CLI tool (no web UI) that executes arbitrary SuiteScript via a local Express proxy and a deployed NetSuite RESTlet.
The execution flow is: CLI (src/commands/run.js) -> proxy (server/app.js /run) -> RESTlet (ns_gm_restlet.js handleRunAction).

The RESTlet injects all 24 N/* modules (including write-capable modules like N/record, N/transaction, N/email, N/workflow, N/task) into the execution scope via `new Function()` (ns_gm_restlet.js lines 71-96, 166).
There is no concept of read-only mode, write mode, or permission levels anywhere in the codebase today.
Credentials are stored as alias-based profiles in ~/.ns-gm/credentials.json with fields: accountId, clientId, certificateId, privateKeyPath, restletUrl, scope (profileStore.js lines 59-66).
The OAuth scope field in profiles is 'restlets' by default (auth.js line 73) - this is an OAuth-level scope, not a read/write permission scope.
The proxy server runs as a detached background process on localhost:9292 (init.js lines 82-88).
Blueprints/product.md line 71 explicitly lists 'No advanced profile permissions model in this phase' as a non-goal.
The prompts library (terminal interactive prompts) is already a dependency, available for building approval flows in the terminal.
helix-ns-server uses ns-gm via setup:ci, selecting PRODUCTION credentials for scout/diagnosis steps and SANDBOX for post-product steps (helix-ns-server credentials.ts lines 11-12, 19-24).
helix-ns-server writes temporary private keys to filesystem, uses them for ns-gm setup:ci, then deletes them (native-phase.ts lines 287-293).

NetSuite OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials (M2M) tokens are scoped at the OAuth level (restlets, REST Web Services) and tied to an Integration record's role - not per-script or per-operation granular permissions.
The RESTlet has no mechanism to distinguish read vs write SuiteScript API calls at the code level before execution.
unknowns: NetSuite does not appear to offer per-script or per-operation granular permissions at the API level. The OAuth token grants full access based on the Integration record's role. How to enforce read-only at the ns-gm/RESTlet layer needs design investigation.
Whether the 'pop-up window' approval UI should be a native OS window (requiring a desktop GUI framework), a terminal-based interactive prompt, a web-based local page, or something else is unresolved.

How to deterministically identify which NetSuite API calls in a script are 'write' operations (record.save(), record.delete(), record.submitFields(), email.send(), transaction.void(), etc.) vs read operations - static analysis vs runtime interception.

How to enforce 'temporary, single-script-only' permission scope: whether the RESTlet should be modified to gate module injection, whether the proxy should intercept, or whether this is enforced purely client-side.
Whether a second NetSuite Integration record (with a write-capable role) is needed for the write-mode credential set, or if the existing read-only role can be temporarily elevated.
Whether the RESTlet needs a second deployment (one read-only, one read-write) or if a single RESTlet can handle both modes.
How the approval state is communicated between the approval UI and the executing CLI/proxy - file-based token, IPC, HTTP endpoint on proxy, or in-process.
What the specific list of NetSuite modules/operations that count as 'write' vs 'read' should be (e.g., is N/https a write operation? Is N/cache?)

Whether the helix-ns-server integration pattern (separate PRODUCTION read-only and SANDBOX read-write credentials) is a viable pattern for this use case or if the ticket specifically requires write to production.
How rollback or undo would work if a write script causes unintended changes.
